text: A particle-filter method that finds the robot's pose in a map that already exists. It is used for localization in a static map. In contrast, SLAM Toolbox is the default SLAM algorithm, used to position the robot and generate a static map.

evidence.quote: technique based on a particle filter, for localization in a static map.
SLAM Toolbox is the default SLAM algorithm, used to position the robot and generate a static map.

text: The coordinate frame rigidly attached to a mobile robot's base. It is part of the tree kept by TF2, the time-variant transformation library in ROS 2. An odometry system gives the odom to base_link transform.

evidence.quote: The tree is kept by TF2, the time-variant transformation library in ROS 2.
The odom to base_link transform is provided by an odometry system.

text: A multi-stage edge detection algorithm that finds thin boundaries. It uses Gaussian smoothing, intensity gradients, non-maximum suppression, and hysteresis thresholding to distinguish true edges from noise.

evidence.quote: to distinguish true edges from noise.

text: A plugin that adds one kind of information, such as lidar obstacles, to a costmap. Layers can also be written to detect and track obstacles using camera or depth sensors, or to change the underlying costmap by some rule or heuristic.

evidence.quote: Layers can also be written to detect and track obstacles using camera or depth sensors, or to change the underlying costmap by some rule or heuristic.

text: An electrostatic discharge vacuum cleaner used to clean accumulated dirt or dust inside the control box. It is built to avoid causing electrostatic discharge (ESD), a static spark that can damage electronics.

evidence.quote: An ESD vacuum is built to avoid causing electrostatic discharge (ESD), a static spark that can damage electronics.

text: An annotated map that marks the areas a costmap filter acts on. Examples include keep-out zones the robot will never enter, speed restriction areas, and preferred lanes for robots moving in industrial environments and warehouses.

evidence.quote: keep-out zones the robot will never enter, speed restriction areas, and preferred lanes for robots moving in industrial environments and warehouses.

text: A formula that counts a mechanism's degrees of freedom from its number of links, joints and joint freedoms. The equation is DOF = m(N − 1 − J) + Σfᵢ. Every link starts with m freedoms, and every joint takes some away.

evidence.quote: Every link starts with m freedoms, and every joint takes some away

text: The costmap layer that adds extra cost around obstacles so the robot keeps its distance. It places a decaying cost around obstacles, which makes it more costly to travel near a collision.

evidence.quote: It places a decaying cost around obstacles, which makes it more costly to travel near a collision.

text: A loom attachment introduced by Joseph-Marie Jacquard in 1804 that used chains of punched cards to control the woven pattern. It was an early example of a machine run by a stored program. Swapping the cards changed the pattern without rebuilding the machine.

evidence.quote: Swapping the cards changed the pattern without rebuilding the machine.

text: The Wireshark display filter protocol name for Modbus/TCP, defining fields including Transaction Identifier, Protocol Identifier, and Length. Technicians can also filter by header values, such as matching a specific transaction identifier.

evidence.quote: Technicians can also filter by header values, such as matching a specific transaction identifier.

text: An industrial communication protocol that carries Modbus messages over Ethernet, using port 502. The TCP/IP version dates from 1999, and the specification is free with no licensing fees.

evidence.quote: The TCP/IP version dates from 1999, and the specification is free with no licensing fees.

text: A robot motion command that interpolates the tool center point along a straight line in Cartesian space. During a joint move, because the joints move together in joint space, the tool tip follows a curved path rather than a straight line.

evidence.quote: Because the joints move together in joint space, the tool tip follows a curved path rather than a straight line.

text: A world-fixed frame in which the robot's pose changes smoothly but slowly drifts. The price is drift, which can grow over time without any bounds.

evidence.quote: The price is drift, which can grow over time without any bounds.

text: A feedback control loop that calculates corrective motor commands to hold a target speed or position. It combines the current error, the accumulated past error, and the error's rate of change.

A URScript function that combines two poses. It is used to convert a pose given in a feature or tool frame into the base frame, for example to compute an approach point. The first argument (the feature) transforms the second argument (the pose relative to the feature) into the base coordinate system.

evidence.quote: The first argument (the feature) transforms the second argument (the pose relative to the feature) into the base coordinate system.

text: A Random Sample Consensus algorithm that finds geometric shapes (such as flat tables) in noisy point clouds. It repeatedly tests random sample points against a distance threshold to ignore outliers. Removing the supporting plane leaves an isolated cloud containing only the elevated workpieces.

evidence.quote: Removing the supporting plane leaves an isolated cloud containing only the elevated workpieces.

text: A URScript command that reads a controller register and returns an integer value between 0 and 65535. Up to 16 binary on/off signals can be consolidated into a single 16-bit register instead of using a separate address for each.

evidence.quote: Up to 16 binary on/off signals can be consolidated into a single 16-bit register instead of using a separate address for each.

text: An axis position counter updated against a synchronization position marking in an ABB robot controller. The first step when updating the revolution counter is to move the robot and positioner axes to their respective zero positions at the synchronization marking.

evidence.quote: The first step when updating the revolution counter is to move the robot and positioner axes to their respective zero positions at the synchronization marking.

text: The Nav2 server that plans through a predefined graph of lanes and nodes, not through free space. The graph can represent lanes, areas the robot is allowed to navigate, or a teach-and-repeat route.

evidence.quote: The graph can represent lanes, areas the robot is allowed to navigate, or a teach-and-repeat route.

text: A control protocol for RC hobby servos where the shaft angular position is proportional to a positive pulse width (1.0 ms to 2.0 ms). The pulse is repeated every 20 ms (50 Hz).

A Nav2 plugin that takes a planned path and returns a smoother, improved one. Smoothers typically reduce path raggedness and smooth abrupt rotations, and they can also increase the distance from obstacles and high-cost areas.

evidence.quote: Smoothers typically reduce path raggedness and smooth abrupt rotations, and they can also increase the distance from obstacles and high-cost areas.

text: A program that is always in exactly one of a fixed set of states (also called a finite state machine). It moves from its current state to another state whenever a given event happens.
A method of controlling a robot remotely in real time by a human operator. A surgeon at a console controls the instruments, so the robot follows rather than acting on its own.
The digital and analog inputs, outputs, and switchable power lines at a robot's wrist connector. They are used to drive and sense a gripper without running external cables along the arm.

The University of Michigan Benchmark is a calibration test for differential-drive mobile robots. The robot drives clockwise and counter-clockwise square paths to separate and measure wheel diameter differences and wheelbase errors.
A robotics approach that uses a camera and vision software to find where a part is. The robot program can then adjust its taught points to match the part's actual position.
A classic PID tuning method based on steady oscillations. It finds the ultimate gain (Ku) and period (Pu), then calculates starting values for the controller gains Kp, Ki, and Kd.

Build a ROS 2 Lyrical Python package from scratch using workspaces and overlays. Topics include ros2 pkg create, setup.py, package.xml, rosdep, colcon, and a timer-driven node that drives Turtlesim in a square.

Explore industrial camera sensors and optical components for machine vision. Key topics include CMOS versus CCD, global and rolling shutters, pixel size, Nyquist resolution, focal length, and telecentric lenses.

Trace the evolution from discrete point-to-point wiring to industrial digital networks. Topics include sinking and sourcing (NPN/PNP), fieldbus history, network topologies, cyclic versus acyclic data, and Device Level Ring recovery.
